subject: Scaling window: pricing options, co-term and invoice split
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@datawave.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, DataWave Procurement <procurement@datawave.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + mid-contract scale: pricing and co-term questions

Hi Ben,

We’re looking to accelerate usage over the next 3 quarters — projected 2.4x consumption for Q1–Q3 next year. We’re mid-contract and would like to: 

- Add a staged uplift now (starting Jan 1) that scales across three windows.
- Co-term the uplift to our existing renewal date (2027-06-30).
- Keep the effective blended unit price within ~10% of our current rate.
- Invoice preferences: procurement wants either a single consolidated invoice or, alternatively, a quarterly split tied to usage buckets.

Can Redwood provide a pricing path that smooths the uplift across the co-term window and propose invoice split options? Also, any docs you can share for procurement (SOW / pricing appendix) would be helpful.

Thanks — want to get a proposal before our exec planning the week of Dec 13.

--
Elena Park
Head of Platform
DataWave
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@datawave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract scale: pricing and co-term questions

Elena — thanks for the context. High level options below; attaching a compact pricing sheet (redwood-pricing-v2.pdf) and a draft SOW to make procurement easier.

Option A — Staged uplift (recommended)
- Immediate top-up that covers Jan–Mar usage (prorated for Jan start).
- Automatic step-up windows in Apr and Jul that align to your volume forecasts.
- Co-term to 2027-06-30; uplift annualized across remaining months so unit rates remain predictable.
- Commercial: 8% uplift discount on the incremental committed volume if you commit to the staged windows (applies to uplift only).

Option B — Voucher smoothing (cash-neutral for you)
- You pre-pay an agreed voucher for uplift capacity; Redwood applies voucher credit monthly to smooth invoice spikes.
- In exchange we can hold the current list rates for 9 months for the uplifted volume.

Option C — Quarterly invoice split (procurement-friendly)
- Consolidated PO but we issue quarterly invoices mapped to usage buckets; we can provide an invoice reconciliation report each month.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Confirm which option you prefer, 2) I’ll send a redline-friendly SOW + pricing appendix, 3) loop procurement for PO details.

If it helps, I can propose a blended example showing exact $/k token across months (I have a working example in the attached pdf).

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-pricing-v2.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + mid-contract scale: pricing and co-term questions — approval request

Team — forwarding DataWave’s ask. My recommended path is Option A (staged uplift with 8% uplift discount) combined with Option C (quarterly invoice split).
Key tradeoffs:
- Option A limits revenue volatility and keeps unit economics predictable; 8% is within my quota authority but if we want to be more aggressive we could go to 10% for a longer voucher commitment (12 months).
- Procurement will push for consolidated invoice; we can do that while still issuing quarterly reconciliations.

Questions: Do we want to offer 10% discount if they pre-pay a 9‑month voucher? Also confirm legal SOW language for co-terming to 2027-06-30 (I’ll ask Legal but want to be sure pricing is aligned).

Thanks — need an approved customer-facing proposal by EOD Monday (13th).

— Ben
From: Elena Park <elena.park@datawave.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: DataWave Procurement <procurement@datawave.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract scale: pricing and co-term questions

Ben — appreciate the quick options. Procurement followed up:

- They prefer Option B (voucher smoothing) to avoid month-to-month reconciliation overhead, but would accept Option A if the discount moves to 12% on the uplift.
- They need a consolidated invoice and PO (we can accept quarterly invoice splits only if the PO covers the full uplift value up front).
- Legal: co-term to 2027-06-30 is fine pending a short SOW amendment; please include a rollback clause if actual usage stays below 60% of forecast at the end of month 3.

Also — procurement is asking whether Redwood can commit to an availability SLA for the uplifted capacity (we’re targeting 99.9% for inference endpoints).

If you can confirm: a revised pricing appendix, an SLA pointer, and a DocuSign-ready SOW, procurement will route the PO next week.

Thanks,
Elena
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@datawave.ai>, DataWave Procurement <procurement@datawave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract scale: pricing and co-term questions — confirmed proposal

Elena — agreeing to a middle path that addresses procurement’s operational preference and keeps us within reasonable commercial exposure. Summary of agreed proposal: 

- Commercials: 10% discount on incremental uplift if DataWave purchases a 9‑month voucher for the uplifted capacity (voucher applied monthly to smooth invoices). This is our final elevated discount for voucher pre-pay.
- Co-term: All uplifted capacity annualized and co-termed to 2027-06-30.
- Invoice: Redwood will accept a consolidated PO (covering voucher amount) and issue quarterly invoices that apply voucher credits; we’ll provide monthly reconciliation reports.
- SLA: Redwood will include 99.9% inference endpoint availability for the uplifted capacity in the SOW; breaches trigger standard service credits per our enterprise SLA schedule.
- Usage rollback: If actual usage is <60% of uplift forecast at month 3, we’ll allow a one-time partial voucher refund for the unused portion (up to 30% of voucher value) or a credit toward future usage — whichever DataWave prefers.

Attachments: updated pricing appendix (redwood-pricing-v2.pdf — updated tab called "DataWave uplift sample"), draft SOW (SOW_DataWave_Draft.docx). I’ll post a DocuSign link once procurement confirms the PO number.

Next steps: 1) Elena — confirm acceptance of the 10% voucher path and PO timing, 2) Procurement — send PO to procurement@redwood.com, 3) We’ll return a DocuSign SOW within 24 hours of PO receipt.

Thanks all — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to review the invoice mechanics.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0179
Attachment: SOW_DataWave_Draft.docx
